layout_details.content: ## 6 Tables

layout_details.content: ## 6.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Tables are coded using XHTML.

layout_details.content: Nested tables are not permitted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The width of the table can be determined with @width and the values indicating the desired width of the table on a page: 33%, 66%, 100%. If there is no indication of @width it means that no specific width is required.

layout_details.content: ## 6.2 Formal and informal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.2.1 Informal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An informal table does not have a caption (label and title) and is captured as a <table> in <array>. It is mostly used to contain structured information presented in tabular format. Its use for keys to formulae is deprecated and has been replaced by <legend>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.2.2 Formal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A formal table consists of a table with a label and a title, captured within <table-wrap>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A table designation is placed above formal tables, e.g. "Table 1- Alphabetical list of definitions".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The two elements that make up the designation, label ("Table 1") and title ("Alphabetical list of definitions "), are tagged inside two different hierarchical elements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Directly below <table-wrap>, <label> contains the label, without punctuation;
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - inside a <caption> element, <title> contains the title.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<table-wrap id="tab-1">

<label>Table 1</label>

<caption>

<title>Alphabetical list of definitions</title></caption>

<table>...

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.3 Table cell styling
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.3.2 @style for borders and background colour
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Borders
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The width and style of individual cell borders can be different from that of the table as a whole and can also vary for each border. @style is used to describe all borders in sequence (order: border-left, border-top, border-right, border-bottom), indicating all values for each before moving on to next (and only if they deviate from the values at the table level).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Borders between adjacent cells have identical values for both cells concerned.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Type / style of border
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When a border is present, its style ("border-style") is indicated with one of these values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - solid
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - dashed
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - dotted
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The words "border-style" are dropped, only the value is given.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Border width
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When a border is present, its width ("border-width") is indicated in px. Preferred values are 1 to 5px.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The words "border-width" are dropped, only the value is given.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Background colour
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If a cell has a background colour, it is indicated in the value "background-color", in hexadecimal values. It is dropped if no background colour is used, except for cases where the table has a background colour defined at the table level - in those cases, the cells with no background colour have the value background-color "none".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - #D4D4D4 - grey
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - #BCBCBC - darker grey

layout_details.content: ## 7.1 Elements and attributes

layout_details.content: ## Editorial note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Numbered formulae usually are separated from the text and labelled with a number in parentheses, e.g. (1). This number is usually sequential and numbered independently throughout the document, irrespective the numbering of any containing clauses. Numbered formulae contained in annexes are prefixed by the annex letter.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A full formula/equation that is separate from the surrounding text is coded using <disp-formula>. If a full formula/equation is embedded in the flow of the text that surrounds it, it should be captured in <inline-formula>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The formula number is captured as a <label> within the <disp-formula>, e.g.

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Definition (<tbx:definition>) - see 9.2.2
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For further information about these and other elements of TBX, see https://www.iso.org/schema/nisosts/v0.2/doc/tbx/index.html.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.2 Definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A definition is coded in <tbx:definition>, inside <tbx:langSet>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A <break/> can be used to insert a line break in a definition if necessary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.3 Terms and additional information on them
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Each term and its descriptive elements are contained in one individual <tbx:tig> (term information group). Terms are coded inside <tbx:term>, which is mandatory.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The elements used to describe terms are currently:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:partOfSpeech>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:normativeAuthorization> (mandatory)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:termType> (mandatory)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:grammaticalNumber> (optional, only on nouns)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:geographicalUsage> and <tbx:grammaticalGender> will probably be used in the future; however, they are not on the roadmap today.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## "Part of speech" of a term
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:partOfSpeech> has the following possible values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - none - in which case the entire element is absent
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - noun
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - verb
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - adj
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - adv
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: electro-pneumatic continuous pressure control valve control valve which continuously modulates the pneumatic power of a system in response to a continuous electrical input signal and which links the electrical input quantity to a pressure value
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.1">

    <label>3.1</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.1">

        <tbx:langSet xml_lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>control valve which continuously modulates the pneumatic power

of a system in response of a continuous electrical input signal and which links the

electrical input quantity to a pressure value</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>electro-pneumatic continuous pressure control valve</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

        </tbx:langSet>

    </tbx:termEntry>

</term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Form of the term (<tbx:termType>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:termType> is optional and can have these values in the ISO/IEC context:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - fullForm (default value, can be omitted)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - abbreviation (for abbreviated forms)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - symbol
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - formula (for chemical formulae)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 3. 13 data monitoring committee DMC independent committee that may be established by the sponsor to assess, at intervals, the progress of the clinical investigation, the safety data or the critical performance endpoints and to recommend the sponsor whether to continue, suspend, modify, or stop the clinical investigation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.13">

    <label>3.13</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.13">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>independent committee that may be...

investigation</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>data monitoring committee</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>DMC</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

                <tbx:termType value="abbreviation"/>

            </tbx:tig>

            </tbx:langSet>

        </tbx:termEntry>

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Term status (<tbx:normativeAuthorization>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:normativeAuthorization> is an optional element indicating the status of a term. It is generally used at ISO/IEC and can have these values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - preferredTerm (recommended)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - admittedTerm (allowed)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - deprecatedTerm (for deprecated or obsolete terms, superseded terms, archaic terms, scientifictechnical slang, terms indicated as "deprecated in this sense" [IEV] and other terms which are detrimental to domain communication)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.9">

<label>3.9</label>

<tbx:termEntry>

<tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

<tbx:definition>radiant power incident on an element of a surface divided by the area of that

element</tbx:definition>

<tbx:source><std id="id-453b14bb-fc43-4d5e-8ff7-bfcdfb4c5fce"><std-id std-id-link-type="urn" std-id-

type="dated">urn:iec:std:iec:60050-731:1991-12::::#con-731-1-25</std-id>

<std-ref> IEC 60050-731:1991, 731-1-25</std-ref></std></tbx:source>

<tbx:tig>

<tbx:term id="ter-irradiance">irradiance</tbx:term>

<tbx:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

<tbx:termType value="fullForm"/></tbx:tig>

<tbx:tig>

<tbx:term id="ter-intensity">intensity</tbx:term>

<tbx:normativeAuthorization value="deprecatedTerm"/>

<tbx:termType value="fullForm"/></tbx:tig></tbx:langSet></tbx:termEntry></term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: and:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.1">

<label>3.1</label>

<txb:termEntry>

<txb:langSet xml:lang="en">

<txb:definition>fluctuating pressure superimposed on the static (barometric) pressure by the presence of sound</txb:definition>

<txb:note id="nte-3.1-1">It is expressed in pascal, Pa.</txb:note>

<txb:tig>
```

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.4 Examples in terminology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Examples in terminology are coded in <tbx:example>. The word "Example" and the number / label are removed from the content. Both need to be added in the rendering process (rule: one example is not numbered, more than one example requires all of them to be numbered, restarting with every term entry).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
3.1 boundaries physical or site limits and/or organizational limits as defined by the organization

EXAMPLE A process; a group of processes; a site; an entire organization; multiple sites under the control of an organization.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.1">

    <label>3.1</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.1">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>physical or site limits... organization</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:example>A process; a group... organization </tbx:example>

        ..

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.5 Notes in terminology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Terminological notes ("Note X to entry") are coded as <tbx:note>. The words "Note X to entry" including the number, are not included in the content and need to be added in the rendering process.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
TERM ENTRY 3.27

TERM NOUN - PREFERRED - FULL FORM

derived class

DEFINITION

class created by inheritance from another class

Note 1 to entry:

Derived class is also named extended class or child class.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="con-3.27">

  <label>3.27</label>

  <tbx:termEntry id="te-3.27">

    <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

      <tbx:definition>class created by inheritance from another class</tbx:definition>

      <tbx:note id="nte-3.27-1">Derived class is also named extended class or child

        class.</tbx:note>

      <tbx:tig id="id-70a027b2-ee5a-4a42-9b6a-fa91d333cf9b">

        <tbx:term id="ter-derived_class">derived class</tbx:term>

        <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

        <tbx:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

        <tbx:termType value="fullForm"/>

      </tbx:tig>

    </tbx:langSet>

  </tbx:termEntry>

</term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.6 Cross-references to terms
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: References to terms in the document can be made
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: a) from one terminological entry to another
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: b) from outside the terms and definitions section
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The two use different tagging.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Cross-references from one terminological entry to another
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Cross-references between terminological entries within the Terms and definitions clause are tagged as <tbx:entailedTerm> with the ID of the referenced entry in @target. This element is only used in child elements of <tbx:termEntry>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 3. 3 correction action to eliminate a detected nonconformity (3.21) NOTE Adapted from ISO 9000:2005, definition 3.6.6.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.3">

    <label>3.3</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.3">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>action to eliminate a detected <tbx:entailedTerm

target="term_3.21">nonconformity (3.21)</tbx:entailedTerm></tbx:definition>

            <tbx:note>Adapted from <std><std-ref>ISO 9000:2005</std-ref>, definition

3.6.6</std>.</tbx:note>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>correction</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

            </tbx:langSet>

        </tbx:termEntry>

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Cross-references from outside the terms and definitions section
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: These are coded in <xref> with @ref-type="custom" and @custom-type="term-entry".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Any data point reporting a concentration below 3 % of the initial concentration (3.1.6) shall be eliminated along with all subsequent data points of the run.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Any data point reporting a concentration below 3 % of the initial concentration (3.1.6) shall be eliminated along with all subsequent data points of the run.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.7 Cross-references to the other sections of the document from the terminology section
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: While previously <tbx:see> was used for references from the terms and definitions to other clauses, tables, figures etc. in the document, now <xref> is used.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.8 Coding the source related to the terminological entry
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If there is a stated source for an entry, it is included in <tbx:source> within <tbx:langSet>. Square brackets and the word "SOURCE" are not included and have to be added during rendering.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 3. 13 lateral position sensor component of the drive unit that provides the lateral position of the measured point Note 1 to entry: The lateral position is customarily measured or inferred by using, for example, a linear encoder, a laser interferometer or a rotary encoder coupled with a micrometer screw. [SOURCE: ISO 25178-600:2019, 3.2.4]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.13"><label>3.13</label>

    <txb:termEntry id="term_3.13">

        <txb:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <txb:definition>component of the drive unit that provides the lateral position of

the measured point</txb:definition>

            <txb:note>The lateral position is customarily measured or inferred by using, for

example, a linear encoder, a laser interferometer or a rotary encoder coupled with a

micrometer screw.</txb:note>

            <txb:source>ISO 25178-600:2019, 3.2.4</txb:source>

            <txb:tig id="term_3.13-1">

                <txb:term>lateral position sensor</txb:term>

                <txb:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </txb:tig></txb:langSet>

        </txb:termEntry>

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.9 Subject fields of a terminological entry
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Subject fields related to a terminological entry are tagged with <tbx:subjectField>, within <tbx:langSet>. Additional punctuation, such as the brackets in the example, have to be added during rendering.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 10.1.8 Footnotes

# Annex A Multilingual contents, translations and adoptions
## A.1 Definitions ## Original standard The document that was developed by ISO or IEC, in the language it was originally developed in ("reference version" in NISOSTS documentation) ## Reference version The original standard in the NISOSTS documentation ## Derived version Document that is based on an original standard but different, e.g. translation, adoption ## Multilingual document Document with more than one language inside the original standard NOTE: Output variants such as PDFs containing different language versions of one original standard do NOT count as multilingual documents. ## Adoption Local version of an original standard It can be - of identical content and in the original language - of identical content and translated - modified (i.e. with additional, modified or deleted content, translated or not) ## Translation Document in a language different from the original ## Localisation Adaptation of content and / or metadata to local specificities ## A.2 Rules of good governance and recommendations for different document categories In this section, we indicate the rules applicable to translations and adoptions of IEC and ISO documents. These are mandatory to follow. All other rules described are suggestions and indicate best practices. Content in the context of multilingualism, translations and adoptions can be of different types: - existing in the original (unilingual) standard and translated exactly - existing in the original standard and modified (added / removed) during the adoption ![](page=27,bbox=[238, 119, 602, 282]) IEC and ISO metadata have to be preserved in any case. A translation of our content has to correspond to the original text. Any modifications of the original content need to be made clear - the status of the document (translated, adopted, modified or not) shall be mentioned. Transparency about the nature of the changes to the original standard (in terms of content or markup) is recommended. Changes should be indicated - in the metadata - in the content in the place where the change has occurred. - in the tagging of the content ## A.3 Structuring and tagging a document ## A.3.1 Structure Organisations adopting an International Standard will use the element (documented on the NISO STS website: https://www.niso-sts.org/TagLibrary/niso-sts-TL-1-2- html/element/adoption.html) to add their own material and, inside , the element to contain the original or translated standard. Inside , the structure of the original standard and its tagging should be preserved. If content is added or modified, the existing tags (elements and attributes) should be maintained; splitting existing tags should be avoided wherever possible. ## Metadata During adoptions, ensure the metadata of originating organisation are preserved, within . Useful tags in this context are (containing metadata valid for the entire document) and (containing metadata for only the derived version). Metadata of the originating organisation must not be modified. When metadata of the adopting organisation are added, these should be contained in , inside . contains information about the table model used, the terminology model and the version of MathML. While NISOSTS allows these to be different at the level of the original standard than in , it is recommended to keep them identical to facilitate the processing of the XML. Avoid , and as they are outdated. For multilingual documents, @xml:lang should be used on the most outer block level element. For example, if a document has alternating sections in English and French, then it is sufficient to provide the @xml:lang="en" or @xml:lang="fr" in the top level element only. ## Elements Content element tags should be maintained whenever the content remains identical. ![](page=28,bbox=[239, 119, 602, 281]) ## Attributes Attributes should be maintained, unless they are directly related to language- or region-specific aspects, as is the case for terminology as coded in TBX and in IEV documents. ## IDs IDs are generally arbitrary, without reproducing semantic meaning, to ensure they can stay identical throughout the document lifecycle even if their purpose or place in the document changes. NOTE: Although many legacy standards still contain semantic IDs,their use is no longer supported. While some may still be present in older documents,all new IDs are generated as arbitrary IDs. For all adoptions or translations of existing content, it is recommended to maintain the original IDs as far as possible (either identical or with a prefix / suffix; in the case of pre-/suffixes, always use the same pattern).
